4073._note: PS Merchant rework 2026-08-09 (the 9 Aug patch notes call it Skeleton Pirate Card): stops granting Discount 5 and becomes the auto-Mammonite card — 5% chance on a physical attack to autocast Mammonite Lv1. The Lv10 upgrade is tagged [Blacksmith] in BOTH the PDF and the patch notes, so it is gated on the job, not on the skill level alone: a Merchant or Alchemist can also master Mammonite (it is a Merchant skill), and would otherwise wrongly get Lv10 procs. Class is the job id — 10 Blacksmith, 4011 Whitesmith. Same shape as Rekenber Mercenary Card's auto-Bash (id 90009). Zeny cost and Zeny Pincher apply in-game; neither is a damage term here. It is also a HEADGEAR card now, not an accessory card (in-game, reported 2026-08-12) — hence the loc override. Both other sources are stale on this: vanilla item_db has EQP_ACC, and the live PS item API still served 'Compound on: Accessory' when checked 2026-08-12, the same lag that left the pre-rework Discount 5 text in ps_item_overrides. loc uses the three head slots, matching every other headgear card in the DB (e.g. Willow 4010). The description is pinned too: the scraped one still described the pre-rework Discount 5 effect, which is plainly wrong now that equipped cards show their description on hover. Text is the live PS item API's (checked 2026-08-12) with one edit — its 'Compound on: Accessory' line reads Headgear, in the client's headgear colour (#6600FF, as on Stainer 4039), since that is the only part the API is still stale on.

81012._note: Description added 2026-08-21 from the live PS item API (tools.payonstories.com/api/pc/item?name=Rust-worn+Apparatus, id 81012) — the item had a manual entry for its script but no description anywhere, so hovering it in the equipment picker showed nothing. Reported by a player, who also thought the Perfect Dodge bonus was missing: it is not, `bonus bFlee2,2` applies and reaches status.flee2 (34 -> 36 on a test Hunter). It simply had nowhere to be SEEN, since the Combat stats panel listed Flee but not Perfect Dodge — now added there. The [Base INT >= 70] clause making Freezing Trap apply Slow instead of Freeze is not a damage term and has no bonus to model, but it is now SURFACED: the engine has no link between a trap and the Frozen target status (Frozen is a manual toggle), so a Hunter who ticked it intending to freeze with Freezing Trap was pricing a state this build cannot produce - and Frozen is worth a lot (element forced to Water, hard DEF halved, auto-hit). BuildEditor warns when Frozen is selected while this item is worn at 70+ BASE INT. A warning, not a block: the target can still be frozen by another source.

2615._note: Safety Ring: PS zeroed the item's structured DEF (its tooltip reads "Defense: 0", scraped faithfully into ps_item_overrides - all 70 def overrides match their own tooltip line) but its description still lists the effects as "Def +3" and "Mdef +3". So the DEF lives in the script, not the def field, and only the MDEF half was modelled - a player reported the ring adding no DEF. bDef and equip DEF both feed hard DEF, so +3 here is what the vanilla item's Def: 3 used to give. NB the only mechanical source for the DEF half is the description prose; the item API does not expose scripts.
